summary: Submitted the direct check for unit-C-append-log-identity-consistency (action=check). Plan (checks/plan.json) and harness (checks/assurance_generated_test.go) exercise the obligation's premise with real target code: a follower whose stored suffix 1..3 (terms 1,1,2) conflicts with an incoming leader term, so DeleteRange(2,3) runs and an injected faithful LogStore fails exactly one StoreLogs call; the handler is driven through the real RPC struct with appendEntries. Prerequisites are conflict_suffix (admitted, node n1, store_logs_failed true) then store_logs_failed (truncated_to correlated to the conflict), and the monitor observes append_probe on the same stream with the oracle accepted==true, identity node, so a rejected probe is a complete violating witness for the bounded liveness responsibility. Construction guidance from a scratch copy of the captured source (draft/tmp/raftbuild, go test with the offline module cache) showed the cached last index remaining 3 while the store's last index became 1 (consistent=false) and the subsequent valid AppendEntries being rejected (accepted=false), which is why the premise warrants an executed clean-copy comparison rather than more reading; that local run is construction knowledge only, not evidence. Grounding cites S-raft-appendentries/S-logstore and the selected binding BND-append-entries-error-return; scope limits (single-shot artificial failure, one follower) are recorded as uncertainties, and no formal finding is claimed. Preflight returned valid:true, so the trusted runner can execute the fixed harness on the captured snapshot.
